title: Universal Log Pre-processing Framework
description:
• Background Modern enterprises generate massive volumes of logs from a wide range of sources, including network devices, servers, operating systems, applications, databases, cloud services, containers, endpoint security tools, identity and access management systems, IoT devices, and other hardware and software platforms. These logs are produced in diverse formats such as Syslog, JSON, XML, CSV, CEF, LEEF, proprietary vendor formats, and application-specific schemas.
The diversity of log structures creates significant challenges in centralized monitoring, security operations, compliance reporting, incident investigation, and threat analytics. Security teams often spend substantial effort developing source-specific parsers and normalization rules before the data can be effectively utilized by SIEM, data lake, or machine learning platforms.
As organizations adopt hybrid, multi-cloud, and AI-driven environments, the need for a universal and extensible log standard that can accommodate both current and future data sources have become increasingly critical.
• Detailed Description Design and develop a Universal Log Pre-processing Framework (ULPF) capable of ingesting, parsing, normalizing, and standardizing logs and events generated by any hardware or software system.
The framework should support diverse event sources while preserving the original event data for forensic and compliance purposes. It should transform heterogeneous logs into a unified schema that enables consistent analytics, correlation, visualization, threat hunting, anomaly detection, and machine learning applications.
The framework must be scalable, extensible, vendor-agnostic, and suitable for deployment in Big Data environments handling billions of events per day.
• Expected Solutions This solution should cover universal event schema and processing framework that enables:
a) Preserve complete raw event data without information loss.
b) Extract and parse source-specific attributes.
c) Normalize fields into a common event taxonomy.
d) Maintain traceability between normalized and original events.
e) Plug-and-play on boarding of new log sources.
f) Unified visibility across enterprise environments.
g) Efficient SIEM and Data Lake integration.
h) AI/ML-ready security and operational analytics.
i) Reduced parser development effort.
j) The solution shall be deployable in an air-gapped network.
k) Solution may be packaged in a container for making it platform independent.
• Current Scope Build a framework that converts any perimeter network device-generated log or event-regardless of source, format, vendor, or technology into a standardized, lossless, analytics-ready representation for next-generation SIEM and cybersecurity platforms.

summary: Innovation (5/5): draws on ai, ml, machine learning applied to a miscellaneous problem, placing it in the breakthrough band. Feasibility (3/5): as a software build with moderate integration complexity, a full build is tight for 36 hours and will need scope-cutting. Impact (2/5): addresses a more targeted user group within Miscellaneous. Tech Depth (5/5): centers on integration, architecture, compliance. Sustainability (3/5): will need a maintenance/upkeep plan post-hackathon. Scalability (4/5): built to extend across states/users with modest rework. Total 22/30 -> Green verdict.

overview.in_plain_terms: Build a framework that ingests logs from many different sources, network devices, servers, cloud services, IoT, in many different formats, syslog, JSON, XML, CSV, and normalizes them all into one consistent structure, so security teams stop building a custom parser for every single log source.
overview.why_it_matters: Security teams currently spend substantial effort building source-specific parsers before data becomes usable in SIEM or ML platforms. A genuinely universal, extensible normalization framework directly eliminates that repeated work.
pain_points: Enterprises generate logs from many diverse sources in many different formats.
Security teams build source-specific parsers and normalization rules repeatedly before data is usable.
No universal, extensible log standard accommodates both current and future data sources.
overview.background: Modern enterprises face genuine complexity from diverse log formats across many sources, requiring substantial repeated parser-development effort before logs can be used for monitoring, compliance, or ML.
overview.whats_being_asked: A Universal Log Pre-processing Framework (ULPF) ingesting, parsing, and normalizing logs from diverse sources and formats (Syslog, JSON, XML, CSV, CEF, LEEF, proprietary) into a consistent, extensible schema.
expected_solution: Multi-format log ingestion (Syslog, JSON, XML, CSV, CEF, LEEF, proprietary).
Automated or semi-automated parsing and field normalization.
Output ready for SIEM, data lake, or ML platform consumption.

analysis.innovation_scope_note: Very High. A genuinely universal, extensible log normalization framework (versus yet another single-format parser) addresses a real, well-articulated, unsolved industry pain point.
analysis.invention_effort_note: High. Requires genuine parsing flexibility across many formats plus a well-designed, extensible schema, real architectural and engineering depth.

competitive_landscape.note: Log normalization tools exist commercially (some SIEM vendors offer this), but a genuinely open, extensible, format-agnostic approach is a real, differentiated technical challenge.

innovation.note: Genuine format-agnostic, extensible log normalization is a real, well-articulated, valuable technical challenge beyond existing single-purpose parsers.

invention.note: Building genuinely flexible multi-format parsing plus a well-designed extensible schema is substantial architectural work.

technical_feasibility.tag: Comfortable for a Scoped Format Subset
technical_feasibility.note: Full coverage of every named format and future extensibility in 36 hours is ambitious; scoping to 4-5 diverse formats with a genuinely extensible schema design is realistic.

impact_and_benefits.note: Directly reduces real, repeated engineering effort for security teams, foundational infrastructure value.

architecture.note: Multi-format parsing feeding a universal schema, genuine architectural sophistication in the schema design specifically.

overall_verdict.reasoning: Strong pick, one of the higher-scoring PS in this batch. The genuine differentiator is your schema design's extensibility, not just how many formats you support, demonstrate that a genuinely new, unseen format can be added without redesigning your core schema.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: Very well-specified list of real log formats gives clear, concrete, checkable technical targets, and this addresses a genuine, well-known industry pain point.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: Building parsers for several formats without a genuinely well-designed, extensible underlying schema would miss the actual architectural point, 'universal' means extensible design, not just format count.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Design your universal schema first, with genuine extensibility principles, before building format-specific parsers, and validate extensibility by adding support for a format you didn't originally plan for and confirming it fits your schema without redesign.

idea_0_4: Design your universal schema first, focusing on genuine extensibility principles (common fields, extensible metadata, format-agnostic core structure).
Choose 4-5 genuinely diverse log formats to build parsers for (Syslog, JSON-based, CSV, and one more structurally different format).
Split: one person on schema design, one on format-specific parser implementation.
prototype_4_22: Build parsers for your chosen formats, mapping each to your universal schema.
Test with real or realistic sample logs in each format.
integration_22_30: Connect all parsers to output consistently into your universal schema.
Test extensibility explicitly: add a new, previously-unplanned format and confirm it fits without redesigning your core schema.
Build basic downstream-consumption demonstration (e.g. simple query/filter across normalized logs from different original formats).
polish_30_36: Polish the framework's usability and documentation for genuine adoption.
Rehearse a live demo showing logs from multiple different original formats appearing consistently normalized.
Prepare to demonstrate your extensibility test explicitly, adding a new format live if possible.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Live-demonstrate genuine schema extensibility, add support for a log format you hadn't planned for at the start, and show it integrates into your existing universal schema without requiring a redesign, that extensibility proof is the actual point of calling this 'universal,' not just supporting several formats you pre-selected.

strengths: Very well-specified, real industry pain point with clear technical targets.
Genuine architectural sophistication opportunity if schema design is prioritized.
weaknesses: Full format coverage isn't achievable in 36 hours, requires honest scoping.
Real 'universal' extensibility requires genuine schema-design foresight, easy to under-invest in favor of just adding more parsers.

team_fit.ideal_ratio: Weight toward schema/architecture design skill, that's the genuine differentiator over a collection of format-specific parsers.
team_fit.approach: Design your universal schema before building any parsers, this determines whether the framework is genuinely extensible or just several parsers bolted together.

ai_buildability_split.ai_can_build_fast: Standard format-specific parsing scaffolding (Syslog, JSON, XML, CSV parsers are well-documented).
ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: Designing a genuinely extensible universal schema that accommodates format diversity without constant redesign, that's real architectural/systems-design judgment.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: An AI-scaffolded collection of format-specific parsers without genuine schema-design thought would just be several separate parsers, missing the actual 'universal' architectural point of this PS.

data_resource_availability.status: Real sample logs in various formats are available from open-source projects, documentation examples, or your own test systems.
data_resource_availability.backup_plan: Construct realistic sample logs in your chosen formats based on real, publicly documented format specifications.

judge_qna.question: How is this genuinely 'universal', not just several format-specific parsers combined?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Demonstrate your extensibility test directly, adding support for an unplanned format and showing it fits your existing schema without redesign, that's the concrete proof of genuine universality.
judge_qna.follow_up: What's the hardest format type your schema would still struggle to accommodate?

judge_qna.question: How does your normalized output actually get used by downstream SIEM, data lake, or ML platforms?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Describe your output format's compatibility with common downstream consumption patterns, and demonstrate a simple query/analysis working consistently across originally different log formats.
judge_qna.follow_up: What normalization decisions did you make that could lose information present in the original format?
